## About me

I am a fourth year PhD Candidate in Biostatistics at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public health (anticipated graduation in May 2027), advised by [Elizabeth Stuart](https://www.elizabethstuart.org/) and [Trang Nguyen](https://nqtrang.com/). My research interests broadly include causal inference, electronic health records, algorithmic fairness, and mental health. My dissertation work focuses specifically on the challenge of unobserved confounding.

<!-- My overall goal is to make causal conclusions drawn from real-world data more reliable, even when key information is imperfectly measured. -->

See my [Student Spotlight](https://publichealth.jhu.edu/2025/student-spotlight-grace-ringlein) to read about my experience in the Department of Biostatistics at Johns Hopkins!
